mechanism: Evaluate relation between two values: Equal, Less, Greater, Incomparable.
invariants: Single outcome: Compare(A, B) returns exactly one of Equal, Less, Greater, or Incomparable.
Operand reversal: Compare(B, A) preserves Equal and Incomparable, and swaps Less with Greater.
Exact equality is transitive; a tolerance-based Equal does not carry this guarantee.
failure_modes: Tolerance chaining: under near-equality A≈B and B≈C without A≈C, so grouping by equality becomes order-dependent.
Undeclared coercion: values are converted by a rule the comparator did not declare, producing Equal, Less, or Greater where its declared relation would return Incomparable.
